# Disney

> [!warning] Fact-check pending
> This page was expanded by a research pass on **2026-07-30** with cited sources, but its
> adversarial verification pass **did not run** (the API spend limit was reached mid-workflow).
> The equivalent pass on the `platform/` pages caught a fabricated statistic, a wrong founder
> attribution and a mis-stated first drop — so treat dates, ownership and figures here as
> **provisional** until verified. See [[log]].


## Overview

Disney is the animation studio and entertainment conglomerate that Walt and Roy O. Disney founded on 16 October 1923, and the `disney` universe here covers its *own* core canon: Mickey Mouse and the Sensational Six, the Walt Disney Animation Studios feature library, the Disney Princess and Disney Villains lines, and the theme parks. It is one of the largest universes in the VeVe catalogue and one of the platform's marquee licences — the Disney × VeVe partnership was announced on 28 October 2021 and launched around the first Disney+ Day.

Disney is unusual in this taxonomy because it sits on **both sides** of the licensing model: it is a licensor in its own right *and* the corporate parent of several other VeVe universes ([[domains/marvel|Marvel]], [[domains/pixar|Pixar]], [[domains/star-wars|Star Wars]], [[domains/20th-century|20th Century Studios]]). See [[#Licensing]] for how those are split.

**On VeVe:** 224 collectibles across 63 sets — browse the [[_index|Collectibles Catalog]] (universe `disney`) or `collectibles.base`.

## History

**Founding and the silent era**

- **16 October 1923** — Walt Disney and his brother Roy O. Disney found the **Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio** in Los Angeles, on the back of a New York distribution contract for the *Alice Comedies*. The company is later renamed the Walt Disney Studio at Roy's suggestion. This date is the company's official birthday, and the anchor for the 2023 centennial.
- **5 September 1927** — **Oswald the Lucky Rabbit** debuts in *Trolley Troubles*. Oswald was created by Disney and Ub Iwerks but distributed through Universal, and the character was lost to Disney in a 1928 contract dispute; the rights only returned to Disney in **2006**. VeVe's *Disney Oswald the Lucky Rabbit — Jump for Joy Character Series* (27 January 2023) is a direct nod to that recovered history.
- **18 November 1928** — **Steamboat Willie** premieres at the Colony Theater in New York: the official public debut of Mickey and Minnie Mouse, and a landmark in synchronised-sound animation.

**Features, parks, and Walt's death**

- **21 December 1937** — *Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs* premieres in Los Angeles — the first full-length cel-animated feature film in English, and the film that funded the studio's expansion.
- **17 July 1955** — **Disneyland** opens in Anaheim, California, beginning the parks business that supplies a large share of Disney's VeVe output (Tomorrowland, Fantasyland, the Haunted Mansion, Disneyland Paris, Hong Kong Disneyland).
- **15 December 1966** — Walt Disney dies of lung cancer at 65. Roy O. Disney carries the Florida project through to completion and dies in **1971**.
- **1 October 1971** — **Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom** opens in Florida; Epcot follows on **1 October 1982** and Tokyo Disneyland on **15 April 1983**.

**Corporate era**

- **1984** — Michael Eisner becomes CEO; the company is renamed **The Walt Disney Company** in **1986**.
- **1989–1999** — the **Disney Renaissance**, the run of animated features (beginning with *The Little Mermaid*) that restored the animation studio commercially. Most of VeVe's Disney feature-film series — *The Little Mermaid*, *Beauty and the Beast*, *Aladdin*, *The Lion King*, *Mulan* — draw on this decade.
- **31 July 1995 / 9 February 1996** — Disney announces and then completes the **$19 billion Capital Cities/ABC** acquisition, adding ABC and a stake in ESPN, and making Disney the world's largest entertainment company at the time.
- **24 January 2006** — announces the acquisition of **[[domains/pixar|Pixar]]** for **$7.4 billion**.
- **31 August 2009** — announces the acquisition of **[[domains/marvel|Marvel]] Entertainment** for **$4 billion**.
- **30 October 2012** — announces the acquisition of **Lucasfilm** — and with it [[domains/star-wars|Star Wars]] — for **$4.05 billion**.
- **14 December 2017 / 20 March 2019** — announces and then completes the acquisition of **21st Century Fox** for **$71.3 billion** after a bidding contest with Comcast, bringing [[domains/20th-century|20th Century Studios]] in-house.
- **12 November 2019** — **Disney+** launches. Its anniversary becomes "Disney+ Day", the hook for the VeVe partnership two years later.
- **2023** — the **Disney100** centennial. Disneyland's celebration opens **27 January 2023**; Walt Disney World's runs **22 September – 31 December 2023**. VeVe mirrors it with the **Disney100 Platinum Moments** range (four sets, March 2023 – December 2023).

## Licensing

- **Licensor:** The Walt Disney Company
- **Parent:** The Walt Disney Company

### Disney as licensor vs. Disney as parent — read this before filing

Disney appears twice in this wiki's data model, and the two roles must not be collapsed:

1. **As a licensor** — the rights-holder VeVe licenses the Disney *core* canon from (Mickey & Friends, WDAS features, Disney Princess, Disney Villains, the parks). Those collectibles carry `universe: disney`, and this page is their domain.
2. **As a corporate parent** — Disney also owns several *other* licensors, each of which is its own universe here with its own domain page and its own drop cadence. On those pages, `licensor` is the studio and `parent` is `The Walt Disney Company`:

| Sibling universe | `licensor` | Acquired | Collectibles |
|---|---|---|---|
| [[domains/marvel\|Marvel]] | Marvel | 2009 | 516 |
| [[domains/star-wars\|Star Wars]] | Lucasfilm / Star Wars | 2012 | 220 |
| [[domains/pixar\|Pixar]] | Pixar | 2006 | 81 |
| [[domains/20th-century\|20th Century Studios]] | 20th Century Studios | 2019 | 224 (see that page) |

So a Spider-Man collectible is Disney-*owned* but is **not** in the `disney` universe; do not re-file it here, and do not "correct" a Marvel page's `licensor` to Disney. Only `parent` should read *The Walt Disney Company*.

**Edge case in the live data:** the `license` field on `disney`-universe items is not uniform — 132 items read `Disney`, 89 read `The Walt Disney Company`, and 3 read `Pixar`. The `Pixar` ones are co-branded Disney·Pixar drops (*Lightyear*, *Up*, the *Disney100 Platinum Moments Pixar Series*) that VeVe filed under the Disney banner rather than the standalone Pixar universe. Treat `Disney` and `The Walt Disney Company` as the same licensor; the split is a source-data artefact, not two entities.

> [!note] Rights are stable here
> Unlike [[domains/star-wars|Star Wars]]-adjacent or Paramount-era licences, Disney's ownership of its own core canon is not in flux — no licensor flag is needed for the `disney` universe. Note only that Disney does not own everything it distributes: *Hocus Pocus 2* and *Wreck-It Ralph* sit inside the Disney canon, while Oswald was outside it for ~70 years.

## On VeVe

Figures below are from the project catalog (`app/data/catalog.js`, universe `disney`) and [[platform/record-sales|record-sales]].

| | |
|---|---|
| Collectibles | **224** |
| Sets | **63** |
| Distinct characters/subjects | **101** |
| First drop | **8 November 2021** (*Walt Disney Animation Studios*, Golden Moments) |
| Most recent drop | **12 April 2026** (*Mickey and Friends — Series 2*, 7 items) |
| Seasons spanned | 3 → 11 |
| Rarity mix | Secret Rare 90 · Ultra Rare 45 · Rare 35 · Uncommon 33 · Common 21 |

**Shape of the licence.** Disney is one of the platform's most *continuously* supported universes rather than a burst licence: 63 sets across roughly four and a half years, averaging a drop or two a month through 2022–2023. The range breaks into four recognisable programmes:

- **Golden Moments** (2021–2022) — the launch programme, gold-statue premiums, including the cross-brand *Disney Duos* and *Golden Moments Finale* sets.
- **Mickey Mouse series 1–4** (Dec 2021 – Dec 2022) — *Steamboat Willie*, *Bandleader Mickey*, *The Sorcerer's Apprentice Mickey*, *Mr. Mouse* — plus *Mickey and Friends* series 1 (2022) and 2 (2026).
- **Parks** — *1955–59 Series*, *Disneyland Resort Tomorrowland / Fantasyland*, *The Haunted Mansion*, *The Art of Disneyland Paris*, *Disneyland Paris 30th Anniversary*, and Hong Kong Disneyland's *Momentous* series. These map onto the parks history above.
- **Feature-film character/accessory/diorama sets** (2023–2025) — the modern template: a 4–5 item character series, a matching accessories series and a single diorama, for *The Little Mermaid*, *Peter Pan*, *Bambi*, *Beauty and the Beast*, *Frozen II*, *Encanto*, *Moana*, *Aladdin*, *The Lion King*, *Wreck-It Ralph*, *Stitch*.

**Scarcest items** (lowest edition sizes in the universe):

| Collectible | Rarity | Editions | Drop |
|---|---|--:|---|
| Faline / Faline's Base | Secret Rare | 118 | 2024-12-22 |
| Wendy | Secret Rare | 153 | 2024-09-28 |
| *The Little Mermaid 2023 Art Series* (4 items) | Secret Rare | 200 | 2023-05-26 |
| Goofy / Pluto | Secret Rare | 228 | 2026-04-12 |
| Thumper / Thumper's Winter Base | Ultra Rare | 342 | 2024-12-22 |
| Smee | Ultra Rare | 353 | 2024-09-28 |

**Largest editions** sit at the other extreme and belong to the early Mickey drops: *A Jaunty Jig* and *Let's Begin!* at **18,928** each, and *Mickey Mouse* / *Minnie Mouse* at **13,928** — edition counts that appear to nod to Mickey's 1928 debut.

**Record sales.** The universe's ceiling is a single item: **The Partners Statue** (Ultra Rare, 4,333 editions, 333 Gems at drop, 12 November 2021 — the Disney+ Day premium), which holds all three of the top recorded Disney sales at **$11,086** (2025-12-14), **$8,999** (2025-09-14) and **$6,800** (2026-03-20). The `disney` universe has **26,136** recorded sales overall, one of the highest sale counts on the platform — high liquidity, but with the top of the market concentrated in the 2021 launch premium rather than in the newer low-edition Secret Rares.

# James Bond

> [!warning] Fact-check pending
> This page was expanded by a research pass on **2026-07-30** with cited sources, but its
> adversarial verification pass **did not run** (the API spend limit was reached mid-workflow).
> The equivalent pass on the `platform/` pages caught a fabricated statistic, a wrong founder
> attribution and a mis-stated first drop — so treat dates, ownership and figures here as
> **provisional** until verified. See [[log]].


> [!note] Licensor — verified 2026-06-25
> Resolved: film rights/creative control with **Amazon MGM Studios** (assumed 24 Mar 2025); Bond IP co-owned by EON/Danjaq (via London Operations LLC). Parent: Amazon.
> Re-checked 2026-07-30: announcement date 2025-02-20, close 2025-03-24, co-ownership and creative control all confirmed — but the JV entity name "London Operations LLC" was **not** re-confirmed and should be treated as unverified. See [[#Licensing]].

## Overview

James Bond is the secret-agent franchise built around Ian Fleming's 007, who debuted in the novel *Casino Royale* (Jonathan Cape, 13 April 1953) and reached the screen in Eon Productions' *Dr. No*, which premiered at the London Pavilion on 5 October 1962 with Sean Connery in the role. It is one of the longest continuously running film series in cinema history, and unusually for a VeVe licence its rights are **split three ways** — trademarks with Danjaq LLC, film copyrights co-owned by Danjaq and MGM, and the literary estate with Ian Fleming Publications — a structure that matters because VeVe's Bond items were licensed under the pre-Amazon MGM/Eon regime.

On VeVe, Bond arrived as a theatrical tie-in: a September–October 2021 partnership with MGM timed to *No Time to Die*, which included the first-ever NFT movie ticket stub. That was followed by the **Bond 60th Anniversary** poster and Legacy Series drops, which ran from October 2022 to December 2023 and then stopped.

**On VeVe:** 49 collectibles across 17 sets — browse the [[_index|Collectibles Catalog]] (universe `james-bond`) or `collectibles.base`.

## History

**The literary Bond**

- **1953-04-13** — *Casino Royale* published in the UK by Jonathan Cape. First print run of 4,728 copies sold out in under a month, and Cape signed Fleming to a three-book deal. This is the franchise debut recorded in `comic_debut`.

**The Eon film series**

- **1962-10-05** — *Dr. No* premieres at the London Pavilion: the first Eon Productions Bond film, produced by Harry Saltzman and Albert R. Broccoli, distributed by United Artists, starring Sean Connery. The Saltzman/Broccoli producing partnership ran until 1975.
- Rights were structured early and have held ever since: **Danjaq LLC**, the Broccoli-family holding company, owns the copyright and trademarks to the screen Bond (including the "James Bond 007" mark and the gun-barrel logo), with **Eon Productions** as its affiliated production arm. The copyrights to the first 20 films are **co-owned by Danjaq and MGM**, the corporate successor to United Artists. Literary copyright sits separately with **Ian Fleming Publications Ltd**.
- **2021** — *No Time to Die*, Daniel Craig's fifth and final outing, reaches cinemas after pandemic delays; it is the film VeVe's first Bond drops promote.

**Amazon acquires the library, then the wheel**

- **2022-03-17** — Amazon closes its acquisition of MGM Holdings for roughly **$8.45bn** (~$6.1bn cash net of cash acquired plus $2.5bn of assumed debt repaid at close), bringing 4,000+ films and 17,000+ TV episodes to Prime Video. This gave Amazon **distribution** rights to the Bond library — not creative control.
- **2025-02-20** — Amazon MGM Studios, Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli announce a **new joint venture to house the James Bond IP**. All three parties remain co-owners; Amazon MGM takes creative control of the franchise. Broccoli said it was time to focus on other projects; Wilson called Amazon MGM "our trusted partner". The transaction **closed 2025-03-24**.
- **2025-06-25** — Amazon MGM names **Denis Villeneuve** director of Bond 26, with Steven Knight writing and Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing.
- **2025-10** — An Eon Productions earnings filing surfaces the figure **$20m** paid by Amazon in connection with the stake/creative-control transfer. Reporting stresses this is best read as an initial payment inside a JV where Amazon holds the majority stake, and Bond outlet MI6-HQ publicly disputed the "producers sold creative control for $20m" framing.

> [!warning] Unverified
> Bond 26 production/release timing and casting are trade reporting only, not studio-confirmed: production is *reported* for 2027 with a *targeted* November 2028 release, and as of mid-2026 the search for a new Bond — reportedly a British actor in his late 20s/early 30s — was still underway with no actor signed. Treat all of that as provisional.

## Licensing

- **Licensor:** Amazon MGM Studios
- **Parent:** Amazon

> [!warning] Licensor flag — rights are split, and VeVe's items predate Amazon's control
> Bond has no single rights-holder. As of 2026: **Amazon MGM Studios** holds creative control and distribution and is a co-owner of the IP through the March 2025 joint venture; **Danjaq LLC / Eon Productions** (the Broccoli family) co-own the IP and hold the screen trademarks; **Ian Fleming Publications Ltd** holds the literary copyright. Every VeVe Bond collectible dropped **before** Amazon took creative control, and the items themselves credit the older chain — the *No Time to Die* drop notes read:
> `NO TIME TO DIE © 2021 Danjaq & MGM. NO TIME TO DIE, 007 Gun Logo, and related James Bond Trademarks TM Danjaq.`
> The 60th Anniversary posters were "commissioned by EON Productions Ltd and Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Studios." So the *licensing counterparty of record* for these collectibles was **MGM + Eon/Danjaq**, and `licensor: Amazon MGM Studios` reflects who controls the franchise **now**, not who signed the VeVe deal. Which entity a future Bond drop would license from is `# TODO`.

**Brand strings in the catalog.** 47 of the 49 records carry the brand `James Bond - 007`; two — the bare "Jet Pack" and "Laser Gun" entries — carry `Amazon MGM Studios`, the only trace of the new owner in the data. Those two share drop date (2023-11-05), edition size (2,007 / 1,007) and price (20 gems) with "Jet Pack from Thunderball, 1965" and "Laser Gun from Moonraker, 1979", so they are most likely **duplicate records of the same two collectibles** rather than distinct items — treat the true distinct count as ~47. Not yet confirmed against the drop notes.

## On VeVe

Real numbers from the project catalog (universe `james-bond`):

| | |
|---|---|
| Collectible records | **49** (across **17** sets) |
| First drop | **2021-10-01** (NTTD: Series 1 / Posters Set 1) |
| Last drop | **2023-12-14** (Bond 60th Anniversary — Legacy Series S002) |
| Rarity mix | 30 Ultra Rare · 12 Rare · 7 Secret Rare — **no Commons** |
| Sum of listed edition sizes | ~104,000 |
| Blind-box items | 16 |
| Seasons spanned | 2–7 |

Notable structural points:

- **No Commons anywhere in the universe.** Bond was drop-priced as a premium licence throughout: NTTD posters at 87–107 gems, the 1:1 Glider at 127/197, the DB5 Interactives at 1,007.
- **A 6% licensor fee applies to Bond secondary-market sales** on top of VeVe's 2.5% — disclosed in the original NTTD drop notes.
- **Two drops line up with the franchise's own calendar.** The NTTD series began 2021-10-01, alongside the film's release window; the 60th Anniversary poster series opened **2022-10-05**, exactly 60 years to the day after *Dr. No*'s London premiere.

The two 7-edition items are the universe's trophies: the DB5 007 Interactive, and the **NTTD Movie Ticket** — the first-ever NFT movie ticket stub, launched 2021-10-06 by MGM and Eon with Cinemark Theatres for seven collectors.

# Jurassic Park

> [!warning] Fact-check pending
> This page was expanded by a research pass on **2026-07-30** with cited sources, but its
> adversarial verification pass **did not run** (the API spend limit was reached mid-workflow).
> The equivalent pass on the `platform/` pages caught a fabricated statistic, a wrong founder
> attribution and a mis-stated first drop — so treat dates, ownership and figures here as
> **provisional** until verified. See [[log]].


## Overview

Jurassic Park is Universal's dinosaur franchise: Michael Crichton's 1990 novel, Steven Spielberg's 1993 film, and the seven-picture, $6-billion-plus series that grew out of it. Its iconography is unusually **prop-driven** — the amber-topped cane, the park entrance gates, the Barbasol shaving-cream cryo-can, Mr. DNA — which is why the VeVe line leans as much on objects as on creatures.

On the platform the franchise arrives in two clearly separated waves: a **Jurassic World Dominion** campaign in mid-2022 timed to that film's theatrical release, and a **Jurassic Park 30th Anniversary** series in 2023 built from artefacts of the original movie.

**On VeVe:** 32 collectibles across 10 sets — browse the [[_index|Collectibles Catalog]] (universe `jurassic-park`) or `collectibles.base`.

## History

**Novel (1990).** Michael Crichton's *Jurassic Park* was published by Alfred A. Knopf in 1990 (399 pp.) and became a *New York Times* bestseller. Universal Pictures acquired the film rights the same year; Crichton did early screenplay work before David Koepp took the script over.

> [!warning] Unverified
> Sources disagree on the **month** of first publication — Wikipedia's infobox reads "October 1990", while first-edition retail records and most secondary write-ups give November 1990. `comic_debut` is therefore held at year precision (`1990`) rather than guessing a month.

**Film (1993).** *Jurassic Park* opened in the United States on **11 June 1993**, directed by Steven Spielberg for Universal Pictures and Amblin Entertainment. It grossed more than $914 million worldwide and was the most successful film released to that point; a 2013 3D re-release pushed it past $1 billion, the first entry in the franchise to do so. At the March 1994 Academy Awards it won all three categories it was nominated in — Best Sound, Best Sound Effects Editing and Best Visual Effects — and in 2018 the Library of Congress added it to the National Film Registry.

**Crichton's sequel and the original trilogy.** Crichton published *The Lost World* in 1995; Spielberg adapted it as *The Lost World: Jurassic Park* (**23 May 1997**). *Jurassic Park III* (**18 July 2001**, dir. Joe Johnston) closed out the first run.

**The Jurassic World reboot.** *Jurassic World* (**12 June 2015**, dir. Colin Trevorrow) restarted the series, followed by *Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom* (**22 June 2018**, dir. J. A. Bayona) and *Jurassic World Dominion* (**10 June 2022**, dir. Colin Trevorrow). *Jurassic World Rebirth* (**2 July 2025**, dir. Gareth Edwards, written by David Koepp) opened to $318.3 million globally — the biggest worldwide studio opening of 2025 — and finished around $869 million. Cumulative franchise box office is over $6 billion.

**Beyond film.** Universal has run Jurassic attractions at its parks since *Jurassic Park: The Ride* (1996), later *Jurassic World: The Ride* (2019) and the *VelociCoaster* (2021) — the same Universal-experiences side of the business that anchors the franchise's licensing programme.

**Why 2022 and 2023 matter for VeVe.** Both drop waves are calendar-locked to Universal marketing beats: the first VeVe Dominion collectible dropped **12 June 2022**, two days after the film's US release, and the 30th Anniversary series landed inside Universal's 2023 programme marking thirty years of the 1993 film.

## Licensing

- **Licensor:** Universal Pictures
- **Parent:** Comcast (NBCUniversal)

VeVe's own drop pages name **Universal Games and Digital Platforms** — the NBCUniversal division that handles licensed games and digital products — as the licensor entity taking the secondary-market cut. Every Jurassic drop page states a **6% licensor fee** on secondary sales, charged on top of VeVe's standard 2.5% secondary-market fee.

> [!warning] Licensor flag
> The **licensor is stable** — Universal has held the film rights since 1990 — but the **corporate parent is moving.** Comcast took control of NBCUniversal in January 2011 (51%) and bought out GE's remaining 49% in March 2013. Comcast then spun its domestic cable networks out as **Versant**, completed 2 January 2026; Universal Pictures, the studios and the theme parks stayed with Comcast. On **29 June 2026** Comcast announced plans to separate **NBCUniversal and Sky** into a new publicly traded company, expected to close in roughly a year and still subject to board, tax and regulatory conditions. `parent` is recorded as Comcast (NBCUniversal) because that is accurate as of 2026-07-30, and should be revisited once that separation closes.

## On VeVe

Numbers below are from this project's catalog (universe `jurassic-park`), not from estimates.

| | |
|---|---|
| Collectibles | **32** |
| Sets | **10** |
| Distinct characters / subjects | 11 |
| Brands | Jurassic World Dominion; Jurassic Park 30th Anniversary |
| VeVe seasons | 4, 6, 7 |
| First drop | **2022-06-12** (Jurassic World Dominion — T. rex) |
| Most recent drop | **2023-11-04** (Jurassic Park 30th Anniversary S2) |
| Rarity spread | 8 Rare, 7 Common, 7 Uncommon, 7 Ultra Rare, 3 Secret Rare |

### Wave 1 — Jurassic World Dominion (Season 4, June–July 2022)

Three character sets, each a four-tier **blind box** at $50 per pull: **T. rex** (12 June 2022), **Blue** (18 June 2022) and **Beta** (16 July 2022). Each set ran Common / Uncommon / Rare / Ultra Rare — the T. rex tiers at 9,250 / 8,250 / 5,250 / 3,250 editions, Blue and Beta at 7,250 / 5,950 / 4,250 / 2,550.

A **Blue and Beta** airdrop followed: snapshot 19 July 2022, distributed **20 July 2022**, awarded by set completion — the top tier went to holders of all three full sets, lower tiers to holders of at least one collectible from each Dominion set. It produced the scarcest Jurassic item on the platform.

Running in parallel, three **cinema promo** sets went out as free redemption codes on **16 June 2022**: AMC Theatres (US), UCI Cinemas Germany, and UCI Cinemas Italy. AMC issued one code per qualifying ticket for the 9 June 2022 Dominion double feature, emailed 16 June with a 16 July redemption deadline, with the three designs assigned at random.

### Wave 2 — Jurassic Park 30th Anniversary (Seasons 6–7, 2023)

Prop-and-creature blind boxes celebrating the 1993 film. **90 editions were reserved** in every case and the first public mint is **#41**.

| Series | Drop | List | Contents (rarity, editions) |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | 2023-08-18, 8 AM PT | $25 | Dilophosaurus (Rare, 1,993) · Mr. DNA (Ultra Rare, 1,393) · Nedry's Computer (Ultra Rare, 1,393) · Cryo-Can (Secret Rare, 993) |
| S2 | 2023-11-04, 8 AM PT | $35 | Jurassic Park Gates (Uncommon, 2,993) · Tyrannosaurus Rex (Rare, 1,993) · Baby Velociraptor in Egg (Ultra Rare, 1,393) · John Hammond's Cane (Secret Rare, 993) |

Every 30th-Anniversary edition size ends in **93** — 993 / 1,393 / 1,993 / 2,993 — against the film's 1993 release year.

| Blue and Beta — Animated 2 | Secret Rare | 424 | 2022-07-20 |

### Supply and burns

The catalog records **179,091 editions issued** across the universe but only **95,152 in circulation** — roughly 84,000 destroyed. Almost all of it sits in the cinema-promo sets, which issued 97,810 and retain 13,878. The extremes are UCI Germany T. rex (10,090 issued, 90 circulating) and UCI Germany Dilophosaurus (2,090 issued, 90 circulating), which is what makes the low-supply Italian promos far scarcer than their headline edition sizes suggest.

> [!warning] Unverified
> VeVe has published no burn statement for these sets. The pattern is consistent with unredeemed promo codes being destroyed after the redemption window closed, but the **cause is inferred, not confirmed.**

### Market notes

- [[platform/record-sales|Record Sales]] has **no per-universe entry for `jurassic-park`** — no Jurassic sale reaches the recorded top-25 window, and the universe is thinly traded compared with Marvel, Star Wars or DC.
- Catalog `floor` values for this universe are lowest **asks**, not traded prices, and on the illiquid promo items they are unreliable — deliberately quoted here as absent rather than as valuations.
- No Jurassic collectible has dropped since **November 2023**, so *Jurassic World Rebirth* (2025) has no VeVe representation at time of writing.

# Marvel

> [!warning] Fact-check pending
> This page was expanded by a research pass on **2026-07-30** with cited sources, but its
> adversarial verification pass **did not run** (the API spend limit was reached mid-workflow).

## Overview

Marvel is the comics-and-cinema universe of Spider-Man, the Avengers, the X-Men, the Fantastic Four and thousands more — begun in 1939 as Martin Goodman's Timely Publications, remade in the 1960s by Stan Lee, Jack Kirby and Steve Ditko, and owned by The Walt Disney Company since December 2009. Its shared continuity was the template the whole superhero-comics industry copied, and the Marvel Cinematic Universe turned that continuity into the highest-grossing film franchise ever made.

On VeVe it is the single largest universe in the catalogue — more collectibles than any other licensor — spanning premium statues, the chibi **Marvel Mightys** line, the **Marvel Metallic Red** con-exclusive variants, crafting/diorama events, and a deep run of artist-cover comic artworks with 1-of-1 Artist Proofs.

**On VeVe:** 516 collectibles across 240 sets — browse the [[_index|Collectibles Catalog]] (universe `marvel`) or `collectibles.base`.

## History

**Timely (1939–1950).** Publisher Martin Goodman founded Timely Publications in 1939. Its first comic, *Marvel Comics* #1, went on sale **31 August 1939** (cover-dated October 1939) and introduced Carl Burgos's android Human Torch and Paul Gustavson's the Angel alongside Bill Everett's Sub-Mariner; the first printing sold out roughly 80,000 copies and a second printing followed. *Captain America Comics* #1 (**March 1941**), by Joe Simon and Jack Kirby, became the line's biggest wartime hit. Some covers cover-dated **November 1948** began carrying a "Marvel Comic Group" identifier.

**Atlas (c. 1951–1957).** Goodman routed distribution through his own Atlas News Company and the comics carried the Atlas globe logo. Superheroes had collapsed commercially; the line survived on westerns, war, romance, crime and monster/sci-fi anthologies — the genre workshop where Lee, Kirby and Ditko built the craft they would reuse.

**The Marvel Age (1961–1970s).** *The Fantastic Four* #1 (**November 1961**), by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby, launched the flawed-heroes-in-a-shared-continuity house style. *Amazing Fantasy* #15 (cover-dated **August 1962**, on sale **10 August 1962**), by Lee and Steve Ditko, introduced Spider-Man. Thor, Hulk, Iron Man, the Avengers, the X-Men, Daredevil and Doctor Strange followed within four years, and the modern "Marvel Comics" brand consolidated over the same period.

**Boom, bust and bankruptcy (1990s).** A speculative comics bubble inflated Marvel's early-90s revenue and then burst. Marvel Entertainment Group filed for Chapter 11 in **December 1996**, and emerged through a contested merger with toy maker **Toy Biz** that produced **Marvel Enterprises** (sources differ on whether the operative date is 1997 or 1998 — see Unverified note below). The rebuilt company licensed its characters aggressively, yielding *Blade* (1998), *X-Men* (2000) and Sam Raimi's *Spider-Man* (2002).

**Marvel Studios and the MCU (1993–).** Marvel Films was incorporated **7 December 1993** and Marvel Studios **7 August 1996**. Marvel Studios' first self-financed film, *Iron Man* (**May 2008**), began the Marvel Cinematic Universe. *Avengers: Endgame* (2019) grossed nearly **$2.8 billion** and was the highest-grossing film of all time from **July 2019 until March 2021**.

**Disney (2009–).** The Walt Disney Company announced its agreement to acquire Marvel Entertainment on **31 August 2009** in a cash-and-stock deal reported at roughly **$4 billion**, and completed it on **31 December 2009** at a final **$4.24 billion**; Marvel shareholders received $30 cash plus 0.7452 Disney shares per Marvel share. In **August 2015** Marvel Studios was moved out from under Marvel Entertainment and placed inside Walt Disney Studios, with Kevin Feige reporting to the Disney Studios chairman. On **29 March 2023** Disney dissolved Marvel Entertainment as a standalone unit, moving Marvel Comics into Disney Publishing Worldwide.

> [!warning] Unverified
> Sources disagree on the exact Toy Biz / Marvel Enterprises date: Wikipedia's *Marvel Comics* article says Toy Biz bought Marvel Entertainment Group in **1997**; secondary write-ups give **June 1998** (merger agreed) and **1 October 1998** (Marvel became a Toy Biz subsidiary and Toy Biz renamed itself Marvel Enterprises). Treat "1997–98" as the safe range until a primary filing is checked. The `1996-12-27` Chapter 11 filing date circulating in blog posts is also not primary-sourced here — only "December 1996" is confirmed.

## Licensing

- **Licensor:** Marvel
- **Parent:** The Walt Disney Company

Marvel is one of the few large VeVe universes with **no rights ambiguity at the top**: Disney has owned Marvel outright since 31 December 2009, and the 2023 restructure moved Marvel's units between Disney divisions without changing ultimate ownership. Two structural caveats are worth recording:

- **Film rights are not merchandising rights.** Sony Pictures has held live-action theatrical film rights to Spider-Man since a 1999 agreement and continues to hold them, which is why Spider-Man films sit outside Disney's distribution even though Spider-Man collectibles are licensed through Marvel. Every Spider-Man item in the catalogue is tagged `licensor: Marvel`. (Reported terms about merchandising rights returning to Marvel in 2015 are widely repeated but not primary-sourced here.)
- **Mixed licensors inside the `marvel` universe.** The catalogue's `marvel` universe contains a handful of items whose per-item `license` is *not* Marvel: four **Stan Lee Universe** items in *Celebrating Stan Lee* (2023-07-18) plus the *Stan Lee Exclusive Fine Art Drop* poster/statue series (2024-07-25); two **Christian Louboutin** items from the *Christian Louboutin and Marvel Limited-Edition Digital Collectible* drop (2023-10-03); one item tagged `Disney` (*Avengers Logo*, 2021-11-10); and one tagged `Universal` (*Blue and Beta — Attack Ready*), which looks like a mis-tag rather than a real Marvel licence.

> [!warning] Licensor flag
> **Stan Lee Universe** — the Stan Lee-branded items filed under this universe are licensed through Stan Lee Universe (the Stan Lee estate joint venture), not through Marvel/Disney. Its ownership and control are listed as in flux in this wiki's licensor-flag set; do not restate Marvel or Disney as the rights-holder for those items.

> [!warning] Unverified
> *Blue and Beta — Attack Ready* is catalogued under universe `marvel` with `license: Universal`. That combination is almost certainly a data-tagging artefact (the characters read as Jurassic World). Flagged for reclassification, not corrected here.

**The first drop.** *Modern Marvel Series 1 — Spider-Man* launched **7 August 2021, 8AM PT** — Marvel's first official NFT collection, five Spider-Man statues at a single tier ladder: *The Amazing Spider-Man* (Common, 32,000 editions, 40 Gems), *Hangin' Out* (Uncommon, 16,000, 50), *Jump Into Action* (Rare, 9,000, 100), *Animated* (Ultra Rare, 2,500, 250) and *Ultimate Animated* (Secret Rare, 1,000, 400). Those 32,000- and 28,999-edition print runs are the largest in the whole Marvel catalogue and have never been repeated at that scale. "Modern Marvel" continued as a numbered statue line — *Alligator Loki* (2021-10-23) is labelled Modern Marvel Series 4.

**Marvel comics.** Marvel's first-ever digital comics arrived on VeVe over three consecutive days in the same month: *Marvel Comics* #1 (**19 August 2021**), *Journey Into Mystery* #85 (**20 August**) and *Fantastic Four* #1 (**21 August**), each in five cover variants — e.g. *Marvel Comics* #1 at 60,000 total editions split Classic 48,000 / Vintage 6,000 / Hero 3,000 / Vibranium 2,400 / True Believer 600. The catalogue's separate **Artist Proof** tier — 82 one-of-one artist artworks, from Skottie Young, Mark Brooks, Greg Land, Russell Dauterman, Marco Checchetto, Adi Granov, Adam Kubert, Peach Momoko and others across 74 artist-cover sets — begins **2022-08-29** (*Black Panther* #25, *Miles Morales: Spider-Man* #25, *Amazing Spider-Man* #1) and is still running in July 2026.

**Marvel Mightys.** VeVe's chibi/big-head figure line and the first Marvel NFT brand created exclusively for the platform. **124 items across 31 sets** carry Mightys branding in the item or set name, spanning **2021-08-14 → 2026-02-14**; 15 of those sets use the explicit `Marvel Mightys - …` prefix (73 items), starting with *Marvel Mightys - Thor* (**2022-06-29**) and running through *Avengers* Series 1–2, *X-Men: Heroes* and *Villains*, *Venomized*, *Symbiote*, *Spider-Man* Series 2, *We Are Groot*, *Strange Tales*, *Fantastic Four* Series 2 and *Celestials* (2026-02-14). The earliest Mightys-named figures (Steve Rogers, Sam Wilson, Bucky Barnes, John F. Walker, Red Skull) shipped inside the *Captain America* drop on **2021-08-14** at 13 Gems.

**Marvel Metallic Red.** A seven-item con-exclusive variant line, every one **Secret Rare** at 444–555 editions: Iron Man (**2024-08-09**, 555 ed, 40 Gems), Thor (2024-08-10, 444), Thanos (2024-08-11, 555), Storm (2024-10-20, 444), Avengers Tower (2024-12-29, 444, 5 Gems), Spider-Man (2025-07-27, 555) and Sam Wilson (2025-10-12, 555). VeVe's own listing for the Iron Man item records 40 editions withheld for licensor/promotional/team use, first public edition **#21**, and MCP priority bidding on the waitlist allocation. Brand page: https://www.veve.me/collectibles/en/brands/71f4a6dc-3aec-4c70-a0b7-4b8c3ac519ad

**Scarcest items.** Beyond the 82 Artist Proof 1-of-1s, the tightest editions are *Spider-Man Noir* (Marvel Mightys - Spider-Man: Series 2, Secret Rare, **88 editions**, 2024-07-13), *Ant-Man - Quantum Realm* (98, 2024-07-27), the *Ghost Rider* craft reward from Marvel Mightys Strange Tales (111, 2024-11-02), *Wolverine - Primal Strike* (150, 2024-07-26) and *Marvel Mightys Groot Captain Marvel* (188, 2024-08-18).

**Record sales.** Marvel leads every universe on [[record-sales]] with **57,227 recorded sales**. Its top three real sales are *Spider-Man: Miles Morales - Animated* at **$14,999** (2026-01-29 — the third-highest sale in the whole catalogue) and *Spider-Man - Ultimate Animated* at **$12,001** (2026-03-20) and **$9,500** (2025-10-24). Both are Secret Rares from 2021-era Spider-Man drops, which is the clearest signal in the data that Marvel's earliest low-edition Spider-Man statues are the franchise's blue chips.

# Pixar

> [!warning] Fact-check pending
> This page was expanded by a research pass on **2026-07-30** with cited sources, but its
> adversarial verification pass **did not run** (the API spend limit was reached mid-workflow).
> The equivalent pass on the `platform/` pages caught a fabricated statistic, a wrong founder
> attribution and a mis-stated first drop — so treat dates, ownership and figures here as
> **provisional** until verified. See [[log]].


## Overview

Pixar is the computer-animation studio that began life inside Lucasfilm, was spun out by Steve Jobs on 3 February 1986, and has been wholly owned by The Walt Disney Company since 5 May 2006. It effectively invented the CG animated feature: *Toy Story* (22 November 1995) was the first feature-length film animated entirely by computer, and eleven Pixar films have since won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. Its characters — Woody and Buzz, Lightning McQueen, Nemo, the *Inside Out* emotions, Mr. Incredible, WALL·E, Carl and Russell — are among the most licensed properties in modern animation.

On VeVe that translates into a broad but per-film catalogue: the studio-wide **Pixar Pals** range, the Disney100 Platinum Moments Pixar series, and dedicated series for *Cars*, *Finding Nemo*, *Up*, *Inside Out*, *The Incredibles*, *Soul*, *Coco*, *Elemental*, *Lightyear* and *Toy Story* — with modern drops running at markedly smaller edition sizes than the 2021–22 wave.

**On VeVe:** 81 collectibles across 25 sets — browse the [[_index|Collectibles Catalog]] (universe `pixar`) or `collectibles.base`.

## History

- **1979** — Lucasfilm opens its Computer Division. Ed Catmull is hired away from the New York Institute of Technology to run its Graphics Group, one of three parts of the division.
- **1982** — the Graphics Group renders the one-minute "Genesis Effect" for *Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan* (1,620 frames, no models or artwork) — one of the first fully computer-generated, fully textured sequences shown in a feature film. (VeVe also carries [[domains/star-trek|Star Trek]] as a separate universe.)
- **1983** — John Lasseter joins the group, hired as an "interface designer", and animates *The Adventures of André & Wally B.*
- **1986-02-03** — Steve Jobs, recently out of Apple, buys the group from George Lucas: $5M paid to Lucasfilm for the technology rights plus $5M of his own cash as capital. The spin-out is named **Pixar** and starts as a *hardware* company, selling the Pixar Image Computer. The short *Luxo Jr.* is released the same year.
- **1988** — *Tin Toy* wins the Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film — the first film made with computer-generated imagery to win an Oscar. It is also the short that draws Disney's interest and seeds *Toy Story*.
- **1991** — Pixar signs a three-picture, $26M deal with Disney.
- **1995-11-22** — *Toy Story* opens, the first entirely computer-animated feature film; roughly $362M worldwide on its initial release. Pixar goes public on NASDAQ as **PIXR** days later, the largest IPO of the year, the stock moving from $28 to $45 inside the first half-hour of trading.
- **1997** — Disney and Pixar sign a 10-year, five-picture co-production pact as equal partners in creation, distribution and marketing; Disney co-finances.
- **2000–01** — the studio moves to its purpose-built campus in Emeryville, California (a second campus building follows in 2011).
- **2004-02** — after about ten months of talks, Jobs walks away from renegotiating with Michael Eisner's Disney. The sticking points: how long Disney would hold rights to future Pixar films, who controlled sequels, and television rights.
- **2006-01-24 → 2006-05-05** — Disney announces, then completes, an all-stock acquisition of Pixar valued at more than **$7.4 billion** (2.3 Disney shares per Pixar share). Jobs becomes Disney's largest shareholder (~7%, ~$3.9B) and joins its board; Ed Catmull becomes president of the combined Disney and Pixar animation studios and John Lasseter chief creative officer.
- **2018-06-19** — Pete Docter is named chief creative officer, succeeding Lasseter.
- **2024-06-14** — *Inside Out 2* opens and becomes the highest-grossing animated film of all time (~$1.69B worldwide), displacing Pixar's own *Incredibles 2* (2018).

Eleven Pixar features have won Best Animated Feature since the category was introduced in 2001: *Finding Nemo*, *The Incredibles*, *Ratatouille*, *WALL·E*, *Up*, *Toy Story 3*, *Brave*, *Inside Out*, *Coco*, *Toy Story 4* and *Soul*.

## Licensing

- **Licensor:** Pixar
- **Parent:** The Walt Disney Company

Unusually for this wiki, the chain of rights here is unambiguous: Pixar has been a wholly-owned Disney subsidiary since the acquisition closed on 5 May 2006, so `licensor: Pixar` / `parent: The Walt Disney Company` needs no flag.

Two practical notes for anyone reading the catalogue:

- The on-chain licence string is **not** consistent — 43 of the 81 Pixar collectibles are tagged `Pixar` and 38 `Disney/Pixar`. Both mean the same rights-holder; treat them as one licensor and filter on `universe: pixar` rather than on the licence string.
- VeVe's own brand hub does not break Pixar out. As of 2026-07-30 `veve.me/brands/` lists Disney (as a licensor) but has no standalone Pixar entry, which is why `veve_url` remains `# TODO` here rather than a guessed slug.

# Star Trek

> [!warning] Fact-check pending
> This page was expanded by a research pass on **2026-07-30** with cited sources, but its
> adversarial verification pass **did not run** (the API spend limit was reached mid-workflow).
> The equivalent pass on the `platform/` pages caught a fabricated statistic, a wrong founder
> attribution and a mis-stated first drop — so treat dates, ownership and figures here as
> **provisional** until verified. See [[log]].


> [!note] Licensor — verified 2026-07-30
> Star Trek is wholly owned by **Paramount Skydance Corporation**: the three-way Skydance Media / Paramount Global / National Amusements merger closed **7 Aug 2025**. Television production and the trademark sit with **CBS Studios Inc.**, a Paramount Skydance subsidiary — the copyright line printed on VeVe's Star Trek collectibles reads "TM & © 2021 CBS Studios Inc."

> [!warning] Licensor flag — corporate parent in motion
> The *franchise* owner is settled; the *corporate parent* is not. Paramount Skydance signed a definitive agreement (27 Feb 2026) to acquire **Warner Bros. Discovery** at $31.00/share. As of 30 Jul 2026 the deal is stalled: 12 state attorneys general sued to block it in July 2026, a federal judge issued a temporary restraining order (20 Jul 2026), and on 24 Jul 2026 Paramount agreed with the state AGs to postpone closing until five days after an antitrust trial or **1 Jun 2027**, whichever comes first. The European Commission cleared it on 22 Jul 2026. Nothing about who owns Star Trek changes if it closes, but re-verify `parent` after the ruling.

> [!info] Name collision — domain vs entity
> Star Trek exists at two levels in this wiki: this universe page and the brand entity [[entities/star-trek|Star Trek (entity)]]. Cross-links must carry a path — `[[domains/star-trek]]` for the universe, `[[entities/star-trek]]` for the brand.

## Overview

Star Trek is the science-fiction franchise Gene Roddenberry pitched to Desilu Productions in 1964 and launched on NBC on **8 September 1966** — now 13 television series (961 episodes across 52 seasons) and 14 feature films. Its premise, a multi-species Starfleet exploring rather than conquering the galaxy, made the ships as recognisable as the crews: the *Enterprise*, the Borg Cube and the Romulan warbird are franchise icons in their own right. That is exactly the angle VeVe took — Star Trek arrived on the platform not as character figures but as a **starship line**, 3D vessels from *The Next Generation* offered in 1:1 and 1:1000 scale, later joined by a *Discovery* fleet.

**On VeVe:** 5 collectibles across 2 sets — see the [[_index|Collectibles Catalog]] (universe `star-trek`).

## History

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 1964 | Roddenberry presents his series treatment to **Desilu Productions** |
| **1966-09-08** | *The Original Series* premieres on NBC with "The Man Trap" (aired two days earlier, 6 Sept, on Canada's CTV). The date is now marked as Star Trek Day |
| 1967 | Paramount absorbs Desilu; Star Trek production continues under Paramount Television |
| 1969 | *TOS* ends after three seasons — syndication reruns build the mass audience |
| 1979-12 | *Star Trek: The Motion Picture* begins the film series (14 features to date, plus TV films such as *Section 31*) |
| **1987-09-28** | *The Next Generation* premieres in syndication with "Encounter at Farpoint", introducing Captain Picard and the Galaxy-class **U.S.S. Enterprise-D** |
| **1988-05-16** | "The Neutral Zone" (TNG season 1 finale) debuts the **Romulan D'deridex-class warbird**, designed by Andrew Probert — his last Star Trek work |
| **1989-05-08** | "Q Who" (TNG season 2) debuts the **Borg** and their cube |
| 1994 | Viacom acquires Paramount |
| 2005–06 | The Viacom/CBS split separates the franchise: CBS becomes titular rights holder (television), Paramount keeps the films |
| 2017-09-24 | *Discovery* premieres on CBS, then CBS All Access → Paramount+; produced by CBS Studios; concludes 2024-05-30 after five seasons |
| 2019-12-05 | ViacomCBS reunites the two halves; renamed **Paramount Global** in Feb 2022 |
| **2025-08-07** | Skydance / Paramount Global / National Amusements merger closes → **Paramount Skydance Corporation**, sole owner of Star Trek |
| 2026 | *Starfleet Academy* premieres 15 Jan 2026 on Paramount+ (renewed for season 2); *Strange New Worlds* season 4 arrives 23 Jul 2026, with a six-episode final season to follow |

All three vessels VeVe minted come from the TNG era: the Enterprise-D (1987), the D'deridex warbird (1988) and the Borg Cube (1989). Those are **on-screen debuts** — the collectibles themselves dropped in 2021–2022 (`comic_debut` vs `nft_drop_date`).

## On VeVe

Figures below are from the project catalog (`universe: star-trek`); the 2026 *Discovery* set is catalogued separately (see below).

- **5 collectibles, 2 sets**, every one a *Star Trek: The Next Generation* starship (brand tag `Star Trek: The Next Generation`, catalog licensor `Paramount`).
- **First drop 2021-09-08** — [[sets/starships-s1|Starships - S1]], 4 items, VeVe Season 2. **Second 2022-09-08** — [[sets/starships-s2|Starships - S2]], 1 item, Season 4. Both landed on 8 September, the *TOS* premiere anniversary / Star Trek Day.
- **37,440 editions minted in total** (31,552 in S1 + 5,888 in S2) — very large runs by later VeVe standards. Lowest public mint on all five is **#41**.
- Each vessel came in two scales: a large **1:1** display model at a premium tier and a **1:1000** miniature at a cheaper tier.

| Collectible | Set | Rarity | Editions | Drop price | Drop |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|---|
| Borg Cube (1:1000) | S1 | Common | 9,888 | 💎40 | 2021-09-08 |
| U.S.S. Enterprise-D (1:1000) | S1 | Uncommon | 8,888 | 💎60 | 2021-09-08 |
| Borg Cube (1:1) | S1 | Rare | 6,888 | 💎110 | 2021-09-08 |
| U.S.S. Enterprise-D (1:1) | S1 | Ultra Rare | 5,888 | 💎130 | 2021-09-08 |
| Romulan D'deridex Warbird | S2 | Ultra Rare | 5,888 | 💎120 | 2022-09-08 |

Scarcest items: the two Ultra Rares — [[collectibles/star-trek-uss-enterprise-d-1-1|U.S.S. Enterprise-D (1:1)]] and [[collectibles/romulan-dderidex-warbird|Romulan D'deridex Warbird]], 5,888 editions each. All five sold out.

**2026 — *Discovery*, at a fraction of the edition size.** A four-ship blind-box set, [[sets/star-trek-discovery-ship-fleet|Star Trek Discovery - Ship Fleet]], dropped **2026-07-05**: *USS Discovery* and *Vulcan Cruiser* (Rare, 550 each), *Klingon Cleave Starship* (Ultra Rare, 275) and *Beacon of Kahless* (Secret Rare, 150, pull odds 1 in 10.22). That is two orders of magnitude scarcer than the 2021 starships. The catalog currently files this set under the `veve-vibes` universe rather than `star-trek`, so it sits outside the 5-collectible count above.

**Market standing.** [[platform/record-sales]] (302,286 real sales analysed since 2025-07-12) has no per-universe section for `star-trek` and no top-25 entry — Star Trek is a small, quiet corner of the platform next to Marvel, Star Wars or DC.

## Licensing

- **Licensor:** CBS Studios (Paramount) — the trademark/copyright line on the VeVe items reads "TM & © 2021 CBS Studios Inc."; the catalog's per-item `license` field records it as `Paramount`.
- **Parent:** Paramount Skydance Corporation (since 2025-08-07)
- **Rights chain:** Desilu (1964–67) → Paramount Television → Viacom (1994) → CBS Corporation after the 2005–06 split, with film rights at Paramount → ViacomCBS (2019) → Paramount Global (2022) → Paramount Skydance (2025). Television production still runs through CBS Studios (with CBS Eye Animation Productions for *Lower Decks* / *Prodigy*).
- The 2021 and 2022 drops were therefore licensed in the ViacomCBS / Paramount Global era; the 2026 *Discovery* set under Paramount Skydance.
- See the licensor flag above for the pending Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition.

# Star Wars

> [!warning] Fact-check pending
> This page was expanded by a research pass on **2026-07-30** with cited sources, but its
> adversarial verification pass **did not run** (the API spend limit was reached mid-workflow).
> The equivalent pass on the `platform/` pages caught a fabricated statistic, a wrong founder
> attribution and a mis-stated first drop — so treat dates, ownership and figures here as
> **provisional** until verified. See [[log]].


## Overview

Star Wars is George Lucas's space-opera saga, launched with *Star Wars* — later retitled *Episode IV — A New Hope* — on 1977-05-25 and grown since into three film trilogies, two standalone features, four decades of animation and, since 2019, a slate of live-action streaming series. Lucasfilm has been a wholly owned subsidiary of The Walt Disney Company since 2012, which makes Star Wars (alongside [[marvel|Marvel]]) one of the two Disney-owned pillars of VeVe's licence book.

On the platform it is the **second-busiest universe by traded volume**, behind only Marvel, and by far the most *format*-diverse: sculpted characters, trooper variants, screen props, helmets, lightsabers, vehicles, buildable dioramas and theatrical-poster art all ship under the same licence.

**On VeVe:** 220 collectibles across 64 sets — browse the [[_index|Collectibles Catalog]] (universe `star-wars`) or `collectibles.base`.

## History

**Original trilogy (1977–1983)** — the three films that established the franchise:

| Film | US theatrical release |
|---|---|
| *Star Wars* (*Episode IV — A New Hope*) | 1977-05-25 |
| *Episode V — The Empire Strikes Back* | 1980-05-21 |
| *Episode VI — Return of the Jedi* | 1983-05-25 |

**Prequel trilogy (1999–2005)** — *Episode I — The Phantom Menace* (1999-05-19), *Episode II — Attack of the Clones* (2002-05-16), *Episode III — Revenge of the Sith* (2005-05-19). This is the era VeVe's Podracer line draws on.

**Animation (2008– )** — *Star Wars: The Clone Wars* premiered on Cartoon Network on 2008-10-03 and ran, after a move to Disney+, to a seventh and final season in 2020; *Star Wars Rebels* followed in 2014 and *The Bad Batch* in 2021. Ahsoka Tano, later a live-action character and a VeVe subject, originated here.

**Disney acquisition (2012)** — Disney announced its purchase of Lucasfilm Ltd. on 2012-10-30 and **closed the deal on 2012-12-21** at a stated value of roughly **$4.05 billion** in cash and stock (Disney issued 37.1M shares plus a $2.2B cash payment). Star Wars, Indiana Jones and Industrial Light & Magic all moved to Disney in that transaction.

**Sequel trilogy and standalones (2015–2019)** — *The Force Awakens* (2015-12-18), *Rogue One* (2016-12-16), *The Last Jedi* (2017-12-15), *Solo* (2018-05-25), *The Rise of Skywalker* (2019-12-20). Thirteen released films have grossed roughly **$10.7 billion** worldwide.

**Streaming era (2019– )** — *The Mandalorian* premiered on **2019-11-12**, on Disney+'s launch day, as the first live-action Star Wars television series; created by Jon Favreau, it introduced Grogu and reset the franchise's centre of gravity from film to episodic television. It was followed by *The Book of Boba Fett* (2021-12-29), *Obi-Wan Kenobi* (2022), *Andor* (2022, with a second and final season in 2025), *Ahsoka* (2023-08-22) and *Skeleton Crew* (2024-12-02).

**Back to theatres (2026)** — *The Mandalorian and Grogu*, directed by Jon Favreau, premiered in Los Angeles on 2026-05-14 and went wide in the US on **2026-05-22** — the franchise's first theatrical release since 2019. VeVe's heaviest Star Wars month on record (May 2026) falls in the same window.

**Comics** — a separate publishing licence with its own history: Marvel launched *Star Wars* #1 in April 1977 and published the title for about nine years; Dark Horse Comics held the licence from **1991 to 2014**; Marvel regained exclusive Star Wars comics rights from **2015** (both publishers being, by then, on either side of Disney's ownership of Marvel); Dark Horse re-took an all-ages/YA Star Wars line from 2022. VeVe's Star Wars poster and framed-art sets are cover/key-art products, not the comics licence itself.

## Licensing

- **Licensor:** Lucasfilm
- **Parent:** The Walt Disney Company

Ownership here is settled and verified — Lucasfilm Ltd. has been a wholly owned Disney subsidiary since 2012-12-21, so no licensor flag is warranted. Two things worth keeping straight:

- The catalogue records this universe's licence string inconsistently — `Lucasfilm (Disney)`, `Lucasfilm (The Walt Disney Company)` and plain `Star Wars` all appear across the 220 items. All three denote the same rights-holder.
- **Comics publishing is a different licence from collectibles.** Marvel's and Dark Horse's rotating Star Wars comics rights (see [[#History]]) say nothing about who VeVe licenses figures and props from — that is Lucasfilm throughout.

## On VeVe

*Catalog snapshot 2026-07-30 (`app/data/catalog.js`); sale figures from [[platform/record-sales]].*

- **220 collectibles across 64 sets**, spanning **VeVe Seasons 3–11**.
- **First drop: 2021-11-11** — C-3PO and R2-D2, issued as part of the cross-brand *Disney+ Golden Moments* promotion (12,333 and 8,333 editions). The universe's first Star Wars-native drop was *Lightsaber Series 1* on 2022-05-26.
- **Most recent drop: 2026-05-31** (BB-8).
- **Cadence by year:** 2 (2021) → 34 (2022) → 31 (2023) → 16 (2024) → 58 (2025) → **79 (2026 to date)**. Output roughly quadrupled from the 2024 trough.
- **Rarity mix:** Common 55, Uncommon 28, Rare 42, Ultra Rare 48, Secret Rare 47 — unusually top-heavy for a VeVe universe, a consequence of the props and trooper-variant sets being built almost entirely out of Rare-and-above tiers.

### How VeVe splits the franchise

Star Wars is the clearest example on the platform of one licence being cut into distinct product formats rather than a single figure line:

| Format | Items | What it is |
|---|--:|---|
| **Troopers** (incl. helmets) | 61 | The dominant line. *Troopers S1–S2*, *Death Troopers S1–S2*, *Night Troopers S1*, *Stormtroopers*, plus the *Edo* stylised troopers — each trooper type reissued in multiple poses (Shooting, Prone, Take Aim, Drawn and Ready) at different rarities. |
| **Posters / framed art** | 32 | *Theatrical Poster Series*, per-film poster series for *A New Hope*, *Empire*, *Return of the Jedi*, the *Holiday Posters*, and *The Mandalorian #1 Framed Art*. Flat art, not sculpts. |
| **Vehicles** | 24 | *Vehicles Series 1–8*: Luke's X-wing, TIE Advanced x1, the AT-AT and AT-ST, T-47 Airspeeder, 74-Z Speeder Bikes, the Series 6 Podracer wave (9 racers) and the Series 8 Millennium Falcon. |
| **Movie props** | 18 | *The Book of Boba Fett — Movie Props* (belt, blaster, chest plate, EE-3 carbine, gauntlets, helmet, jetpack), *Death Trooper Movie Props*, *Hoth Diorama — Movie Props*. Individual pieces of kit sold separately, each at its own rarity. |
| **Trooper helmets** | 10 | *Trooper Helmets Series 1–3* — including a cross-section cutaway and a Series 3 of four battle-damaged Stormtrooper helmets (Blasted, Cut, Gouged, Stabbed), all Secret Rare at 501 editions. |
| **Dioramas** | 9 | *Jawas*, *The Mandalorian*, *Podracers*, *HOTH Battlefield*, *Hangar Bay 327*. |

Two structural patterns are visible in the data:

1. **Diorama + accessories.** A diorama drops alongside a same-day accessory set that populates it — *Hangar Bay 327* and *Hangar Bay 327 — Accessories* (Battery Box, Fuel Drum Stack, GNK Power Droid, Hangar Walkway, all Rare at 777) both landed 2026-05-04.
2. **Edition sizes that quote the films.** The Series 8 *Millennium Falcon* is 1,977 editions with a companion *Holodisk* at **77** (A New Hope, 1977); the 2026 *Yoda* and *Boba Fett's Helmet* are both 1,980 (The Empire Strikes Back, 1980).

Eras covered: original trilogy (the *A New Hope*, *Empire* and *Return of the Jedi* collections), prequels (the Podracer wave, Mace Windu), *Solo* (Mimban Trooper), sequels (Kylo Ren's Lightsaber, BB-8), and the Disney+ era — *The Mandalorian* (Grogu, IG-11, the Armorer, Beskar Ingots), *The Book of Boba Fett*, *Obi-Wan Kenobi* (Reva, Haja Estree, L0-LA59 Lola, Inquisitor Scythe starfighter) and *Ahsoka* (Night Troopers).

### Scarcity

- **Scarcest item: IG-11 — Assassin Droid, 19 editions** (2026-05-30) — the smallest Star Wars edition on the platform.
- A **50-edition tier** sits just above it: the *Edo* trooper variants (Imperial Royal Guard, Scout Trooper, Stormtrooper), *Alert — Special Edition*, and two Secret Rare Boba Fett props (Belt, Jetpack).
- Most of the sub-100 items are **blind-box chase pulls** from trooper sets — Death Trooper and Troopers S2 "Prone"/"Shooting" Secret Rares at 66 editions, the Darth Vader Samurai *Wrath of the Dragon* at 77.
- At the other extreme, the 2022 lightsabers were mass drops: *Yoda* at 19,800 and *The Skywalker Lightsaber* at 19,770.

### Market

Star Wars has recorded **53,300 completed sales** since 2025-07-12, second only to Marvel (57,227). Highest real sales on record for the universe:

| Price | Collectible | Rarity | Sale date |
|--:|---|---|---|
| **$11,204** | [[stormtrooper-rotj\|Stormtrooper]] (Return of the Jedi, dropped 2024-03-24) | Common | 2026-06-01 |
| **$9,301** | [[boba-fett-i-have-you-in-my-sights\|I Have You In My Sights]] | Ultra Rare | 2026-02-17 |
| **$7,538** | [[yoda-star-wars-yoda-2026\|Yoda]] | Common | 2026-05-12 |
| **$6,999** | [[darth-vader-the-emperors-fist\|The Emperor's Fist]] | Ultra Rare | 2026-02-21 |

The $11,204 Stormtrooper is a **top-25 all-time sale platform-wide** — and a Common, which shows how much of Star Wars price discovery runs on mint number rather than rarity tier.

# Tarzan

# TMNT

> [!warning] Fact-check pending
> This page was expanded by a research pass on **2026-07-30** with cited sources, but its
> adversarial verification pass **did not run** (the API spend limit was reached mid-workflow).
> The equivalent pass on the `platform/` pages caught a fabricated statistic, a wrong founder
> attribution and a mis-stated first drop — so treat dates, ownership and figures here as
> **provisional** until verified. See [[log]].


> [!note] Licensor — verified 2026-06-25
> Resolved: **Nickelodeon**, under **Paramount Skydance Corporation** (merger completed 7 Aug 2025).

## Overview

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is the mutant-vigilante franchise created by Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird, launched in May 1984 as a self-published black-and-white Mirage Studios comic with a print run of 3,000 copies. A 1987 Fred Wolf animated series and the Playmates toy line turned that indie one-shot into one of the largest licensing properties of the late 20th century — roughly US$1.1 billion in Turtles toys sold between 1988 and 1992 alone — and the 1990 live-action film became the highest-grossing independent film to that point at over US$200 million worldwide. Viacom's Nickelodeon bought the global rights from Laird's Mirage Group and 4Kids Entertainment in October 2009, and the property now sits inside Paramount Skydance Corporation. On VeVe, TMNT is a *multi-year* premium program launched 8 November 2025 with Paramount, built around the four brothers plus dioramas, props and vehicles.

**On VeVe:** 25 collectibles across 13 sets — see the [[_index|Collectibles Catalog]] (universe `tmnt`).

## History

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 1983 | Eastman and Laird sketch the first "Ninja Turtle" during a late-night drawing session in Northampton, Massachusetts. |
| Mar 1984 | Mirage Studios founded. |
| May 1984 | *Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles* #1 self-published in oversized magazine format, 3,000-copy print run, debuted at a comic convention in Portsmouth, New Hampshire; sold out. Intended as a one-shot. |
| 1987 | First animated series (Fred Wolf Films) premieres; Eastman and Laird license the characters to **Playmates Toys**. Playmates sells ~US$1.1B in Turtles toys 1988–1992. |
| 1990 | First live-action film, with suits from Jim Henson's Creature Shop — >US$200M worldwide, then a record for an independent film. |
| 2003–2009 | *Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles* animated series on FoxBox/4KidsTV, produced by 4Kids Entertainment and co-produced by Mirage. |
| 21 Oct 2009 | Peter Laird / the Mirage Group and 4Kids sell the **global TMNT rights to Viacom's Nickelodeon** for a reported **US$60 million**. Laird retained a clause allowing up to 18 black-and-white TMNT comics per year through mainstream publishers. |
| Aug 2011 | **IDW Publishing** takes the comic licence; Kevin Eastman returns as co-writer and artist. |
| Sep 2012 | Nickelodeon's CGI-animated series premieres — five seasons through 2017. |
| Aug 2014 / Jun 2016 | Live-action reboot (dir. Jonathan Liebesman, Michael Bay producing) and sequel *Out of the Shadows*. |
| Aug 2023 | *Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem* (dir. Jeff Rowe, prod. Seth Rogen). |
| 2024 | *Tales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles* premieres on Paramount+; cancelled in 2025 amid post-merger management changes. |
| **7 Aug 2025** | **Paramount Skydance Corporation** formed from the merger of Skydance Media, Paramount Global and National Amusements — TMNT is among the IP that passes to David Ellison's company. |
| 8 Nov 2025 | **First VeVe TMNT drop** — the *Born Below* dioramas, announced as a multi-year VeVe × Paramount program. |
| Nov 2025 | *Rise of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles* (and *Dora*) cancelled at Paramount. |
| Feb 2026 | Paramount announces a franchise-wide push: *Teeny Mutant Ninja Turtles* YouTube series (2026, Nickelodeon Digital Studio), *Mutant Mayhem 2* (2027), an untitled live-action/CG hybrid film (2028), Mattel toy lines from 2027, and new publishing. |

## Licensing

- **Licensor:** Nickelodeon — holder of the global TMNT IP since the 21 Oct 2009 purchase from Mirage/4Kids.
- **Parent:** Paramount Skydance Corporation (formed 7 Aug 2025; Nickelodeon sits under Paramount Media Networks within its TV Media segment).

> [!warning] Licensor flag — which Paramount label is the licensor?
> The *corporate parent* is settled, but the **contracting label is not consistently recorded**. VeVe's own launch post credits "**Paramount**", while the catalog's per-item `license` field is split across **Nickelodeon** (12 items) and **Paramount Pictures** (4 items), with 9 items blank. Post-merger, brand management is described as running through Nickelodeon and a Paramount global products & experiences group. Treat any single label on an individual TMNT collectible as provisional until VeVe's per-item metadata is normalised; the domain-level `licensor`/`parent` above are the verified values.

## On VeVe

TMNT arrived on VeVe on **8 November 2025** as a **Season 11** franchise, announced jointly with Paramount as a multi-year premium program and given a full public launch at DesignerCon Las Vegas the following week. Per the project catalog (universe `tmnt`): **25 collectibles across 13 sets**, 23 of them with confirmed edition sizes.

**Shape of the program.** Every Turtle ships as a repeating four-piece template — a `Classic` (Common, 2,987), a `Classic (Special Edition)` chaser (Common, **87**), an `IncogNinja` variant (Ultra Rare, 487), and a themed **base diorama** (Uncommon, 3,987, 10 Gems) that the figure stands on. Character drops listed at **40 Gems**; the *Born Below* dioramas at **30 Gems**.

| Drop | Release |
|---|---|
| 2025-11-08 | [[sets/teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-born-below\|Born Below]] — Gold Diorama (Secret Rare, 87) + Silver Diorama (Common, 1,987) |
| 2025-11-29 | [[sets/teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-michelangelo\|Michelangelo]] + Skate Jam Base |
| 2026-01-03 | [[sets/teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-leonardo\|Leonardo]] + Tactical Dojo |
| 2026-04-04 | [[sets/teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-raphael\|Raphael]] + Tune-Up Workshop |
| 2026-04-22 | [[sets/teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-origin-diorama-props\|Origin Diorama Props]] — Mutagen, Pizza Boxes, Rat, Sewer Manhole (all Common, 1,987) |
| 2026-06-17 | [[sets/turtle-cycle\|Turtle Cycle]] (Common, 1,987) |
| 2026-07-04 | [[sets/teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-donatello\|Donatello]] + Laboratory Lounge — completing the four brothers |

**Scarcity.** Almost every edition size across the franchise ends in **87** — 87 / 487 / 887 / 1,987 / 2,987 / 3,987 (the lone exception found is Master Splinter's 28-edition Zen Pose). The scarcest `tmnt`-tagged items are the four `Classic (Special Edition)` chasers and **TMNT — Born Below (Gold Diorama)** (Secret Rare), all at **87 editions**; the `IncogNinja` Ultra Rares sit at 487.

**Market.** [[platform/record-sales|Record Sales]] logs **12,979** recorded TMNT sales in its window (from 2025-07-12), topped by:

| Price | Collectible | Date |
|--:|---|---|
| **$7,576** | [[collectibles/leonardo-classic-2026-01-03\|Leonardo - Classic]] | 2026-01-05 |
| **$5,128** | [[collectibles/leonardo-classic-special-edition\|Leonardo - Classic (Special Edition)]] | 2026-01-04 |
| **$3,504** | [[collectibles/michelangelo-classic-special-edition\|Michelangelo - Classic (Special Edition)]] | 2025-12-06 |

> [!note] Catalog data note — universe tagging
> Several TMNT releases are catalogued under other `universe` slugs (notably `real-world-brand`) rather than `tmnt`, so the 25/13 figures **undercount** the franchise. Those include the whole **Master Splinter** set (drop 2026-08-02: Zen Pose 28 · Battle Ready 287 · IncogNinja-tier Combat Training 487 · Weapon Training 887 · Father Figure 2,987 · B&W Variant 87), **Sewer Manhole - Gold** (87), **Turtle Catapult** (2,987, 2026-07-29) and a second **Turtle Cycle** (2,987). # Catalog Backlog & Coverage

## How many collectibles are there? (researched 2026-06-24)

| Bucket | Estimate | Notes |
|--------|---------:|-------|
| **Total distinct collectibles tracked** | **~8,800** | Veve Alpha's live tracker figure (figures + statues + art + comics that trade secondary). *(high conf the figure exists)* |
| **Comics** | **~5,000–6,000** | VeVe Comics launched Mar 2024 (300+ day one), weekly since. The majority of the 8,800. *(deferred — owner said comics later)* |
| **Non-comic collectibles** (figures/vehicles/art) | **~2,500–4,000 (best ~3,000)** | The 3D premium line since Oct 2020. *(medium conf)* |
| **Catalogued so far** | **1,091** | batches 1–9 (as of 2026-06-25) |
| **→ Non-comic remaining** | **~1,400–2,900 (best ~1,900)** | the long tail: minor variants, craft/accessory items, smaller licensors, 2025–26 drops |

So we're at roughly **~30–40%** of the non-comic catalog. "8M+ NFTs sold" elsewhere = *editions*, not distinct designs — ignore for catalog sizing.

> [!success] Coverage state (2026-06-25)
> **Deep per-universe enumeration** (hand each research agent its universe's "already have" list, ask only for verified net-new) is the working method. The **big universes are now deeply covered**: Marvel (200+), Disney (120+), Pixar (75+), Star Wars (95+), DC (75+), real-world-brand (150+: USPS/Coca-Cola/stamps), veve-vibes (110+: BLACKPINK/Ron English), tokidoki (40+). **Confirmed COMPLETE:** Star Trek (5/5, TNG-only), Ghostbusters, Street Fighter (SFV roster only). The remaining non-comic tail is smaller licensors + 2025–26 drops + craft/accessory/diorama variants. **Next frontier = the comics corpus** (still deferred).

> [!note] To get exact figures-vs-comics counts
> The community trackers (vevesetlist, ecomiwiki, veverank) are JS-rendered SPAs — read their per-category filters in a real browser (Chrome MCP) to convert these estimates into hard numbers.

## How the rest get filled
1. Run more ingest batches (parallel research agents → `/tmp/collectibles_batch*.data` → `/tmp/gen_batch3.sh`, which dedups by slug **and** content-key).
2. Authoritative per-item source: `https://www.veve.me/blog/collectibles/<slug>` (pre-2023: `medium.com/veve-collectibles`).
3. Each new collectible auto-joins its character entity + set on the next `gen_entities_from_collectibles.sh` / set-field pass.
4. Then **comics** as a separate corpus.

## Confirmed NOT on VeVe (don't chase)
He-Man/MOTU, Care Bears, Transformers, G.I. Joe, SpongeBob, Sanrio/Hello Kitty, Pac-Man, Pokémon — all on other platforms. ThunderCats = comics only. **Added by batch 6–9 research:** Bugatti/McLaren/Pagani/Pininfarina (automakers — only Lamborghini + Maserati are on VeVe); Ice Age, Planet of the Apes, Family Guy, Futurama, Bob's Burgers, Aliens-vs-Predator; classic Ultraman (Taro/Tiga/Z) + classic kaiju (Zetton/Baltan/Red King/Gomora) = manga only; The Boys + VIZ = comics/manga only; NFL + Fast & Furious = unverifiable as VeVe drops.

> [!note] Correction (batch 6)
> **Avatar: The Last Airbender IS on VeVe** — Aang & Katara dropped 2026-03-14 (a prior version of this page wrongly listed it as absent). It is a distinct universe from James Cameron's *Avatar*.

## Known future leads (exist but unverified — for a later pass)
- **TMNT:** Donatello, Splinter, Shredder, April, Krang, Bebop/Rocksteady — announced/planned, not yet minted (Season 11 rollout ongoing).
- **Predator "Jungle Predator"** 3D figure set — signalled, per-item data not yet published.
- **DCon Vegas 2025** VeVe Originals (Roth Rind, Nick Walker, Sket One, Tara McPherson, etc.) — announced, no edition/price data yet.
- **tokidoki** Tokimondo Kaiju, Mermicorno Phygital — exist but data unconfirmed.
